subject: Fw: side by side boxplots for non mutually exclusive categories

messages.subject: Fw: side by side boxplots for non mutually exclusive categories
parts:
Ah. I see. The first email from Quentin, the data frame is created differently using yes/no. In his follow-up, in which he's found a solution, he creates mydata as follows:

blueEyes <- sample(size=50,c("BlueEyes","notBlue"), replace=TRUE)
brownHair <- sample(size=50,c("BrownHair","notBrown"), replace=TRUE)
age <- rnorm(50, mean=50, sd=20)
mydata <- data.frame(indiv=1:50,blueEyes, brownHair, age)

So anyways, for what it's worth, that's why my code didn't work. It doesn't work with the data frame he supplies in his first email, but does work using the second one.

ggplot(mydata, aes( blueEyes, age) ) +
geom_boxplot( data = drop.levels( subset( mydata, blueEyes == "BlueEyes") ) )+
geom_boxplot(data = drop.levels( subset( mydata,brownHair == "BrownHair") ) ,aes( brownHair, age)) +
labs (x="Characteristic")

What I was looking for, why the question interested me, was whether or not there was a way to cast or recast the dataset above so that it's molten, in which case there'd be no need for creating distinct data frames, or for subsetting the data as I've done. Although, molten data would include in addition to the ages of brown haired and blue eyed people, those of people without either blue eyes or brown hair.

 



Adam Loveland

dear, all,
I finally found a solution,  not very elegant because it requires the
creation of a dataset per characteristic. maybe someone else will need
this or maybe someone will think of a less verbose code.

First, code  presence/absence with specific names for each variable:
blueEyes <- sample(size=50,c("BlueEyes","notBlue"), replace=TRUE)
brownHair <- sample(size=50,c("BrownHair","notBrown"), replace=TRUE)
age <- rnorm(50, mean=50, sd=20)
mydata <- data.frame(indiv=1:50,blueEyes, brownHair, age)

Then, create subdataframes for the presence of each characteristic :
data1 <- subset(mydata, blueEyes=="BlueEyes")
data1$blueEyes <- droplevels(data1$blueEyes)

data2 <- subset(mydata, brownHair=="BrownHair")
data2$brownHair <- droplevels(data2$brownHair)

create the plot by adding the 2nd dataset with a new call to
geom_boxplot:
p <- ggplot(aes(x=blueEyes, y=age), data=data1) + geom_boxplot() +
geom_boxplot(aes(x=brownHair, y=age), data=data2)
p + xlab("")

This is what i wanted. Thank you

Quentin
PS:  i was also told that using the package gridExtra might help.



On Nov 3, 7:32 pm, Quentin Vincent <quentin.vinc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi everyone,
>
> I have variables coding for a presence/absence characteristic (eg
> brown hair yes/no; blueEyes yes/no).
>
> These characteristics are non mutually exclusive (unlike the usual
> levels of a single factor).  you can have both brown hair and blue
> eyes.
>
> I'd like to plot age distributions for the presence of each
> characteristic on one plot, with a unique age axis. (ie 2 boxplots,
> distributed as follows :  one tick for blueEyes:yes, one tick for
> brownHair:yes)
>
> I can't figure out how to do it.
>
> Here is an example :
> blueEyes <- sample(size=50,c("yes","no"), replace=TRUE)
> brownHair <- sample(size=50,c("yes","no"), replace=TRUE)
> age <- rnorm(50, mean=50, sd=20)
> mydata <- data.frame(indiv=1:50,blueEyes, brownHair, age)
>
> I can get a plot with 2 boxplots according to the presence/absence of
> each characteristic.
> ggplot(aes(x=blueEyes, y=age), data=mydata) + geom_boxplot()
> ggplot(aes(x=brownHair, y=age), data=mydata) + geom_boxplot()
>
> I'd like to have side by side the "yes" boxplot of each of the two
> plots above.
>
> Thanks for your help!!
>
> Quentin
